title: Agent Optimization with Pydantic AI: GEPA, Evals, Feedback Loops — Samuel Colvin, Pydantic
talk_summary: Samuel Colvin demos using Pydantic AI evals, GEPA prompt optimization, and managed variables to improve an agent's accuracy from 85% to 96.7% on a structured extraction task. The practical loop is: build a golden dataset, run deterministic evals, let a proposer agent mutate prompts, and deploy winning configs via managed variables/AB targeting.

takeaways.what_they_do: They load cases with golden outputs, run the agent with prompt/model overrides, score with custom deterministic evaluators, and compare runs to inspect individual failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can have a like deterministic eval like this where we're comparing what the result is versus a golden data set, that's much better.
takeaways.numbers: 85% initial prompt, 92% expert prompt, 96.7% GEPA on 65 test cases; full run 650 MPs

takeaways.technique: GEPA prompt optimization with proposer agent
takeaways.what_they_do: A proposer agent generates new prompts from eval feedback; candidates are scored against a dataset and recombined from the Pareto frontier.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ask an agent to generate a new prompt, if it does better, take bits of that, put it into a new prompt

takeaways.technique: Optimize prompt for cheaper model, then route
takeaways.what_they_do: They use prompt optimization to make a dumber/faster/cheaper model perform a narrow task, rather than always using the strongest model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: get a dumber model or a faster model or a cheaper model to be able to do some task, they make a lot of sense.
takeaways.numbers: Shopify example: $5M/year to $73k/year; 98% private data claim

takeaways.what_they_do: Prompts, model choice, and temperature are stored as typed managed variables; percentage targeting lets them canary new values without redeploying.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can basically define what percentage of calls are using which of our different values

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat what the user does next as stronger evidence than thumbs up/down, because explicit feedback is rarely clicked.
takeaways.evidence_quote: single best way of getting of evaluating the performance of a given question response pair is to look at what the user did next

takeaways.technique: Select prompt snippets instead of appending
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting the optimizer generate an ever-longer prompt, split instructions/examples into selectable pieces and optimize which subset to include.
takeaways.evidence_quote: split your system prompt up into like 200 sentences and say which is the best 20 sentences to use.
